To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lepton flavor violating decays $\mu \rightarrow e \gamma$, $e \rightarrow e \nu$ are sensitive to the leptoquark couplings to leptons and quarks.

the experimental data on the LFV decays $\mu \to e \gamma, \tau\to \mu \, \gamma, \, \tau \to e \, \gamma$ can be explained by the existence of light leptoquark states with masses below $1\,\mathrm{TeV}$. This is a new result, which is in contrast with the previous literature on the topic.
Scalar leptoquark contributions into $l_i→l_j\gamma$ processes are considered.

the scalar leptoquark contributions into $l_i \to l_j \nu_k \bar{\nu}_k$ processes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leptoquarks are not ruled out, and that they are still viable as a source of lepton flavor violation.
there is no compelling theoretical reason for believing that there is a single mechanism for the generation of the masses and mixings of quarks and leptons, and that there are several possibilities.

the leptoquark model under discussion can explain the experimental results on the decays $l_i \to l_j \ gamma$ and at the same time is consistent with the existing experimental data on the processes $e^+e^- \to e^+e^-,\ e^+e^-\to \mu^+\mu^-,\ e^+\ e^- \to \tau^+ \tau^-$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scalar leptoquark contributions to the decays $\tau \to l_i \gamma (l_i \neq l_j)$ can be large and comparable to that of the standard model (SM) contributions.

the leptoquark model can provide the correct order of magnitude of the decay rates of the LFV processes $l_i\rightarrow l_j\gamma$, while the lepton flavor mixing angles can be of order $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$.
the scalar leptoquark contribution into $l_i \to l_j \nu_k \bar \nu_k$ decays are suppressed, but the scalar leptoqurak contribution into $l_{i}\to l_j\, \gamma$ decays are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scalar leptoquark contribution to $l_i\rightarrow l_j\gamma$, $l_i\neq l_j$, decays is suppressed by the lepton Yukawa couplings.
the scalar leptoquark contribution to $l_i\rightarrow l_j\gamma $ is suppressed by the lepton mass.
